To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
dietary arginine restriction significantly reduced the rate and extent, and increased the tumor latency, of two-stage epideral carcinogenesis in mice.
dietary arginine restriction reduced ornithine and putrescine in the epdiermis of CD-1 mice, and reduced tumorigenesis and tumor putrescine levels in the two-stage model of carcinogenesis.

dietary restriction of arginine, the precursor of ornithine (a substrate of ornithine decaboxylase, the rate-limiting enzyme in polyamine biosynthetic pathway), reduced the level of ornithin and putrescine in the epdermis of mice and inhibited the development of skin tumors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of ornithine and putrescine in the initiation and progression of epidermal tumors.
the role of ornithine and its metabolite, putrescines, in two-stage mouse skin carcinogenesis.
the effect of dietary restriction on polyamine biosynthesis and tumorigenisis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
dietary restriction of arginine, and the resultant decrease of ornithine and putrescine, inhibits epidermal carcinogenic progression.
dietary arginine restriction, in this animal system, appears to reduce the extent of epidermal tumorigenesis by reducing the availability of ornithine for polyamine biosynthetic reactions.
dietary arginine restriction significantly reduces ornithine levels and ornithine-derived putrescine in epidermal tissue and inhibits the induction of skin papillomas by TPA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

dietary arginine restriction can alter the ornithine and putrescine levels in epidermis, reduce the rate of epidermal cell proliferation and tumorigenisis and that this effect may be reversed by the addition of ornithin to the drinking water.
the dietary approach of arginine restriction can reduce ornithine and putrescine levels in the skin of mice and inhibit tumor development in this animal model of skin cancer.

the dietary restriction of arginine to the mouse resulted in an inhibition of ornithine and putrescine synthesis in the epidermal tissue, and this was associated with a decrease in the rate and incidence of tumor promotion and a prolongation of tumor latency.
The main takeaway from our work is that
arginine restriction can reduce the rate of tumor formation in the two-stage mouse skin model of carcinogenesis.
dietary restriction of arginine reduces ornithine and putrescine in the skin of mice and that the reduction in putrescine reduces tumour formation.
dietary arginine restriction is an effective means of inhibiting ornithine decaboxylase (ODCase) activity and putrescine levels, and thus inhibits tumorigenesis.
